- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates downside; add buffer below forecast or adjust downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; align forecast with sentiment reversal within 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; increase forecast volatility or add mean-reversion term if sentiment is neutral.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment ≤ 0.33), model often fails to capture downward drift; apply downward bias or adjust for low conviction.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in linear trends; introduce curvature or stepwise adjustments based on sentiment momentum.
